final.title: Spot trial expiry before it becomes a surprise
final.body:
If you run a small business, spotting trial expiry early is a bounded workflow decision, not a grand AI project: when should an alert fire, and who should see it first? The useful diagnostic is simple. Are the trial dates already in one place, like a calendar, email, spreadsheet, or CRM, or are they scattered across vendor accounts? If they are central, a basic reminder may be enough. If they are scattered, you may need a small integration, but still only for one repeatable job.

Keep the human in charge. The alert should surface the date; the owner still decides whether to renew, downgrade, or cancel. That is the right boundary, because money movement and other high-risk decisions stay with a person. Automation can reduce the chance of a missed deadline. It should not quietly choose the plan. That is how you end up with a very efficient surprise.

One practical next step: list every SaaS trial you are using and note which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. That inventory tells you whether the problem is simple monitoring or a small custom workflow in your own environment. Bareni’s role is to help define that boundary clearly, not to skip past it.
